subject: Confirming data handling & training exclusion after demo — Vectra Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire O'Neil <claire.oneil@vectrahealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Oct 2025 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick follow-up + summary from today's demo

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the items you asked us to confirm:

- Training-on-customer-data: Redwood supports an explicit opt-out so customer inputs (prompts, files, outputs) are not used to improve or fine-tune any shared models. We can provide a signed statement you can attach to your procurement package.
- Logs & troubleshooting: We keep request/response logs for troubleshooting by default. You asked whether we can limit retention and restrict access to a small set of people.
- Data residency: You need data to remain in us-east (AWS us-east-1) for processing and storage.
- Retention window: Vectra requested a 90-day retention for non-PII logs and a different handling path for PII.

Attached is a short PDF that summarizes our defaults and the DPA snippet we usually include for training exclusions. Can you confirm the following so we can lock these into the SOW and DPA?

1) Confirm that Vectra wants model-training excluded for all customer content sent to Redwood (prompts, files, embeddings).
2) Confirm the retention window for logs (you proposed 90 days) and whether certain PII fields must be redacted before logging.
3) Confirm data residency requirement (us-east-1) and whether backups must also be resident there.

Next steps from our side once you confirm: we’ll prepare a short opt-out addendum and route to legal + security for signing, and we will open an internal ticket to configure regional processing and the retention policy in the sandbox environment.

Attachment: [Attachment: Redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (PDF, 38KB)]

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Claire O'Neil <claire.oneil@vectrahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@vectrahealth.com <security@vectrahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Oct 2025 10:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + summary from today's demo

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our security team (copied):

- Yes, Vectra requests a formal opt-out: no customer content may be used to train shared models or to update any public weights. We will need a signed addendum for procurement.
- Retention: 90 days for request/response logs and metadata is acceptable for now. We also require that any PII (full names, SSNs, MRNs, patient identifiers) be redacted before logs are persisted. If redaction is not feasible at the platform layer, then logs must be gated and only readable by a named small set of Redwood SREs with justification tracking.
- Data residency: Confirmed — all processing and backups must remain in us-east-1.

One more question: do you store any model-generated embeddings or derivatives beyond raw text? If so, are those covered by the same opt-out?

We need the DPA snippet and the signed opt-out addendum to move to PO. Our procurement timeline is tight — if we can get the addendum signed by Oct 14 we can be on the November onboarding.

Thanks,
Claire
Director of Product, Vectra Health
claire.oneil@vectrahealth.com

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + summary from today's demo

Ben / Evelyn —

Short internal note before we reply to Claire:

- Embeddings/derivatives: anything derived from customer content (embeddings, reranking indexes, finetune artifacts) are considered part of customer data. For an opt-out we mark those data paths as "no-train" and block them from joining any model-improvement pipelines. They will still be stored if the customer requests features that require them (e.g., semantic search); storage retention follows the same retention policy.
- PII redaction: We do not currently do automatic PII redaction across arbitrary uploads. Options for Vectra: 1) client-side redaction before sending, 2) apply server-side redaction via a managed ingest pipeline (we can run a redaction plugin in the us-east sandbox for an additional professional-services setup), or 3) accept gated logs (restricted ACL + audit trail).
- I attached the DPA snippet we typically use that covers training exclusions and the config steps for retention & region.

Attachment: [Attachment: DPA_training_exclusion_snippet.pdf (PDF, 4KB)]

Proposed reply: confirm the opt-out for training including embeddings/derivatives, confirm 90-day retention with PII redaction requirement (ask whether they want managed redaction or gated logs), and confirm data residency and backup requirement. Also propose to add a security call (30m) this week to get their security team comfortable.

I'll stand by to create the internal ticket to lock region + retention once Claire confirms the redaction approach.

-Rohan
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire O'Neil <claire.oneil@vectrahealth.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, security@vectrahealth.com <security@vectrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + summary from today's demo

Claire —

Thanks — this is all straightforward and we can accommodate Vectra's requests. Confirmations below so procurement has explicit language to accept: 

- Training exclusion: Redwood will not use any Vectra customer content (including prompts, uploaded files, model outputs, embeddings, or any derivatives) to train or improve shared/public models. This includes embeddings and reranking artifacts; those will be excluded from any model-improvement pipelines. We will provide a signed opt-out addendum for your contracts team.

- Logs & PII: Default request/response logs are retained for 90 days for troubleshooting. Per your requirement, PII as defined (names, SSNs, MRNs, patient IDs) will not be persisted in logs unless redacted. Since you indicated client-side redaction may be difficult, we propose gated logs: logs are persisted but encrypted and access-controlled; access is limited to named Redwood SREs and requires documented justification. If you prefer managed server-side redaction, we can scope PS work and provide costs.

- Data residency: All processing and backups for the Vectra account will be confined to AWS us-east-1. We will not replicate or back up to other regions.

Next steps:
1) I'll attach the formal DPA snippet and the opt-out addendum to this thread and route to legal for signature (DocuSign link will follow).
2) Rohan will open RED-11234 to configure region + retention and the gated logs ACL.
3) Suggesting a 30-minute security sync this week — let me know times that work for you and your security contact.

Attached: [Attachment: Redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (PDF, 38KB)] [Attachment: DPA_training_exclusion_snippet.pdf (PDF, 4KB)]
Links: https://support.redwood.com/tickets/RED-11234, https://docusign.com/embedded?token=3f7a9c

If that language looks good I will convert it into an addendum and send for signature.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
